_source: RFC 8785 sections 3.2.2, 3.2.3 and appendix B, extracted mechanically from https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785.txt. Do not hand-edit.
_note: The AAD and the JWK thumbprint are both taken over this canonical form, so a library that is only nearly JCS produces an envelope that opens under one build and not another. The sorting case is the sharp one: it puts a non-BMP code point (U+1F600) beside U+FB33, where code point order and UTF-16 code unit order disagree.

sorting.input_source:
{
"\u20ac": "Euro Sign",
"\r": "Carriage Return",
"\ufb33": "Hebrew Letter Dalet With Dagesh",
"1": "One",
"\ud83d\ude00": "Emoji: Grinning Face",
"\u0080": "Control",
"\u00f6": "Latin Small Letter O With Diaeresis"
}
sorting.why: The input is kept as JSON SOURCE because the RFC prints it in an order you must not trust; expected_property_order is the RFC's own answer.

sample.why: input_source is JSON source, not a parsed value: 333333333.33333329 has to be parsed and rounded to 333333333.3333333 by the canonicalizer. Pre-rounding it here would make the case test nothing. stringify_output is what the RFC says a plain JSON.stringify() gives -- correct numbers, input property order -- so it is NOT the canonical form; canonical is the sorted one from 3.2.3, and that is what we must produce.
